comparison: Both address genome assembly and annotation (C21-C27). OpenEval finds the statistics and methodology well-supported and internally consistent. Peer reviewers accept the assembly but request more details about the annotation pipeline, specifically about Trinity transcript rejection rates and Augustus model verification beyond training.

Both evaluate differential expression analysis (C28-C37). OpenEval finds the RNA-seq analysis, statistical testing, and functional enrichment well-supported. Peer reviewers question the GO/PFAM categorization methodology, requesting more objective assignment of categories and expressing concern about subjective decisions introducing bias in the 'larger groupings' approach.
OpenEval finds alternative splicing analysis (C38-C43) well-supported with appropriate methodology and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

Both address alternative splicing validation and analysis (C44-C49). OpenEval finds the thresholds, RT-PCR validation, GO enrichment, and statistical testing well-supported. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about this analysis, indicating acceptance of the methodology and conclusions.

Both address differential splicing analysis (C50-C52). OpenEval finds the validation rate and functional interpretation appropriately cautious and well-supported. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without raising specific concerns.

Both address lincRNA identification and characterization (C53-C59). OpenEval finds the pipeline, filtering steps, and statistical comparisons sound. Peer reviewers accepted the lincRNA findings without requesting additional validation or methodological clarification.

Both address lincRNA conservation analysis (C60-C62). OpenEval finds the statistical testing and comparative analysis well-supported, with appropriate contextualization of negative results. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns about these findings.

Both address lincRNA differential expression and specificity (C63-C65). OpenEval finds the statistical testing and quantified comparisons appropriately cautious. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without specific concerns.

Both address lincRNA expression correlation with neighboring genes (C66-C67). OpenEval finds the statistical testing appropriate and conclusions well-supported. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about this analysis.

Both address lincRNA structural and regulatory features (C68-C71). OpenEval finds the thresholds appropriate and conclusions logically derived with cautious language. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without specific concerns.

Both address comparative transcriptomic analysis across species (C72-C76, with R5 also including C5, C128). OpenEval finds the methodology sound despite varying sample numbers. Peer reviewers question the framing as 'species-specific cell type evolution,' suggesting the evolutionary interpretation needs reconsideration in view of biological functions.

Both address correlation with human proliferative cells (C77-C80). OpenEval finds the PCA and GO enrichment well-supported with appropriate contextualization. Peer reviewers question the novelty, noting that conserved proliferation genes are known from yeast studies, and request clarification of what was already known.

Both address co-regulation analysis of integrin adhesome (C81-C85). OpenEval finds the correlation analysis well-supported with appropriate explanations for exceptions. Peer reviewers praised this as 'perhaps the most interesting findings' providing 'meaningful insight' through 'creative analysis.'

Both address absence of ECM components (C86-C88). OpenEval finds the negative findings appropriately interpreted with cautious language. Peer reviewers accepted this analysis as part of the praised integrin adhesome findings.

Both address co-regulation of filopodial and synaptic machinery (C89-C91). OpenEval finds the contrast between ancestral co-regulation and lack thereof striking and well-supported. Peer reviewers praised this analysis alongside the integrin adhesome findings.

Both address secretome analysis (C94-C101). OpenEval finds the combined experimental and computational approaches comprehensive with appropriate qualification of conclusions. Peer reviewers accepted the findings but requested terminology clarification, preferring 'fungal-like' or 'osmotrophic' over 'fungal.'

Both address trypsin evolution analysis (C102-C106). OpenEval finds the multi-faceted analysis (proteomic, genomic, phylogenetic, expression) well-supported. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the secretome analysis.

Both address LGT detection and characterization (C107-C112). OpenEval finds the phylogenetic methods and transcriptional support rigorous. Peer reviewers requested verification that LGT genes are on same scaffolds as eukaryotic genes; the 87.7% transcriptional support appears to have satisfied contamination concerns.

Both address CotH gene evolution (C113-C118). OpenEval finds the phylogenetic analysis and functional interpretation well-supported with appropriate caution. Peer reviewers' contamination concerns appear addressed by transcriptional evidence.

OpenEval finds the main synthesis claims (C2-C4, C119) about complex gene regulation well-supported by multiple analyses. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these synthesis claims.

Both address secretome and adaptation synthesis (C6, C120, C126). OpenEval finds the characterization as 'fungal-like' appropriate given convergent evolution. Peer reviewers accepted the data but requested terminology clarification.

Both address independent evolution of multicellularity (C5, C128). OpenEval finds the conclusion supported but notes alternative interpretations cannot be ruled out. Peer reviewers question the 'species-specific cell type evolution' framing, suggesting reconsideration in view of biological functions.

Both address evolutionary inferences about animal ancestors (C7, C121, C130). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the conflation of complexity in extant species with ancestral capabilities. Peer reviewers challenge the phylogenetic framing, requesting more accurate divergence time estimates and clearer articulation of relationships.

Both address interpretation of stages as analogous to cell types (C122-C125). OpenEval finds the analogy appropriately cautious and the temporal separation inference reasonable. Peer reviewers explicitly challenge conflating 'stages' with 'cell types,' noting functions are temporally separated, not spatially segregated, and requesting more in-depth discussion.

Both address ancestral co-regulation claims (C127). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that observation in extant species requires phylogenetic reconstruction for ancestral inference. Peer reviewers challenge the phylogenetic framing and evolutionary interpretation more broadly.

Both address the integration model for animal multicellularity (C129). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is speculative and one of several possible interpretations. Peer reviewers challenge the evolutionary framing and request more careful contextualization of phylogenetic relationships.

Peer reviewers accepted the basic characterization of Creolimax and developmental stages (C1, C14-C20), with minor comments about analogies. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically evaluates these organism description claims.
